query: For titanium alloys used as structural materials, formulate one hypothesis for an intervention that could increase surface hardness and wear resistance. Specify the intervention, its proposed mechanism, the expected improvement relative to the untreated alloy, the service or test conditions under which the effect should hold, prior evidence supporting the hypothesis, and a controlled experiment with clear results that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The surface hardness and wear resistance of titanium alloys can be increased through the incorporation of aluminum and other elements, such as vanadium, into the alloy matrix.
generation.material_initial_state: Titanium alloy in its untreated state
generation.intervention: Incorporation of aluminum and other elements, such as vanadium, into the alloy matrix
generation.conditions: Under various wear conditions, including dry and lubricated environments
generation.structural_mediator: The presence of aluminum and other elements, such as vanadium, which can promote hardness and wear resistance
generation.mechanism: The solid-solution strengthening effect of aluminum and other elements, such as vanadium, on the titanium alloy matrix
generation.predicted_outcome: An increase in surface hardness and wear resistance of the titanium alloy
generation.boundary: The limit of the alloy's wear resistance, beyond which the incorporation of aluminum and other elements no longer provides significant improvement
generation.uncertainty: The optimal amount and distribution of aluminum and other elements required to achieve the desired improvement in wear resistance, as well as the potential effects on other material properties, such as ductility and toughness

falsification_experiment.design: A controlled wear test, in which the titanium alloy with and without aluminum and other elements is subjected to various wear conditions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the incorporation of aluminum and other elements does not result in a significant improvement in wear resistance, as measured by the wear rate and coefficient of friction, then the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text: Experimental research on HEA as a reinforcing medium is in the growing stage where several researchers tried different HEAs as reinforcements and reported better properties. Analysis of Cu- AlCoNiCrFe HEA composite fabricated through powder metallurgy reveals that the composite has no evidence of unwanted grain growth and intermetallic phase formation while the yield strength of copper was found to increase with HEA addition. An enhancement in hardness of 63.7% was achieved when CoCrFeMnNi was reinforced with Al 2024 alloy. Utilization of Al0.3CoCrFeNi HEA particles as reinforcement in copper matrix resulted in an improvement of wear resistance. Investigation of the effect of AlCrFeMnNi HEA on the Aluminum MMC reveals that hardness and wear resistance increase with the increase in HEA particle. Fe29Cr28Mn19Ni18Al5Si reinforced Al MMC shows the addition of HEA in the aluminum matrix has a significant influence on friction coefficient. Various studies on HEA-reinforced composites have already proven HEA as a potential reinforcement material for composite fabrication whereas its effect on wear resistance of test composite at different sliding conditions is not explored in detail. Figure 5 and Figure 6 show illustrative results of the measurements of the wear rate on the friction paths for Al alloy and vanadium alloy, respectively. In the analyzed case, the tests were conducted under identical parameters for both materials. Therefore, linear wear, represented by the depth of the groove (friction track) in the radial section, was used for comparison. Friction tests were conducted under identical conditions for both alloys. With a sliding speed of 0.1 m/s and a time of 1800 s, the friction path was 180 m, which, with a friction radius of 3 mm, results in approx. 9550 friction cycles. A comparison of the width of the friction paths in Figure 5 and Figure 6 shows that the friction trace is much narrower for the vanadium alloy. The groove depth was measured on a measuring microscope. The results of the tests are summarized in Figure 7 along with the materials’ hardness measurements. The addition of vanadium resulted in an increase in the hardness of the alloy by 33% and a significant decrease in friction wear value by 73%.

One of the most investigated HEA systems is AlCoCrCuFeNi and the copper-free derivate AlCoCrFeNi [,]. Distinct improvement of mechanical properties can be achieved by alloying with titanium. Due to its large atomic radius, the addition of titanium causes solid–solution strengthening and hence increased strength and hardness. Additionally, the formation of brittle phases was observed for a high content of titanium [,,]. The wear resistance of the alloy system AlCoCrFeNiTi has been investigated under various conditions revealing an increased wear resistance, also in comparison with the steels EN 1.3505 and EN 1.3343 [,]. Although improved high-temperature properties of AlCoCrFeNiTi are expected, the wear behaviour has not yet been investigated at increased temperature.
